summary: Every digit copy must be inspected, establishing an Omega(n) input-reading lower bound, and the accepted frequency algorithm matches it before scanning a fixed decimal candidate domain.

optimality.argument: Changing any unread input digit can create or remove valid numbers, so a correct algorithm must inspect all n positions. The reference builds ten frequencies in one pass and performs only 450 fixed-value candidate checks afterward.

replacement_checks.evidence: An adversary can change an uninspected digit copy and alter whether a required hundreds, tens, or units value is available, so all n entries must be read.
The accepted source performs one O(n) frequency pass followed by at most 9 * 10 * 5 constant-domain digit triples using constant storage.

Authored cases cover leading zeroes, zero as an even units digit, insufficient and excess duplicate copies, no even digits, every decimal digit, and maximum input length; the certificate regression checks every legal digit multiset.
